title: SAML assertion ordering + session stitching causes transient admin privilege or unexpected permission denial
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary: Several customers reported either 'permission denied' errors for users who should have access or, conversely, brief elevated privileges after SSO events. Root cause appears to be an ordering edge in the SAML attribute processing + session stitching flow used by RBAC v2 when multiple identity providers (IdPs) and transient session attributes are present.

What happens today: when a login or assertion arrives we merge assertion attributes into an existing session. The merge path does not consistently apply deny-over-allow precedence and can retain stale transient roles from a prior session if the new assertion arrives with a subset of attributes. In some traces the audit log only records the successful assertion, not the state removed during merge, making post-incident analysis hard.

Why this is bad: customers intermittently receive denied API responses for actions they routinely perform, causing escalations. In other cases elevated privileges linger for short windows, which fails our least-privilege guarantees and is a compliance risk.

Scope: Reproduced on hosted and dedicated (internal prod-like) environments. Affects SAML and some SSO providers that send overlapping group and role assertions and when session TTLs allow stitched merges. Not related to the RBAC policy language itself, but how session attribute precedence and audit writes occur during assertion processing.
repro_steps: 1) Create two distinct IdP assertions for a single user: one with admin-like transient role, another later without that role but with overlapping group attrs. 2) Log in via IdP1 (admin role) and perform actions to confirm admin access. 3) Before session TTL expires, trigger a login via IdP2. 4) Observe session merge: in broken path the old transient role can persist or the new assertion can suppress an allow incorrectly. 5) Capture /api/v1/session and /api/v1/audit logs for the times around both assertions.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Session merge follows deterministic ordering: explicit denies take precedence over allows; transient roles from previous sessions are cleared unless reasserted. 2) Audit logs contain a before/after snapshot for any session attribute changes caused by an assertion merge. 3) Regression tests cover multi-IdP merge ordering and prevent reintroduction. 4) Fix deployed to staging and validated by SE on two customer escalations reproductions. 5) No increase in request latency for assertion processing beyond 5ms median.
implementation_notes:
- Normalize attribute canonicalization early (lowercase keys, canonical group IDs).
- Add a merge strategy that computes resulting role set by: base_roles + explicit_assertion_adds - explicit_assertion_removes, then apply deny-first resolution using policy engine.
- Persist an audit row showing 'session_pre_merge_attrs' and 'session_post_merge_attrs' (JSON string) with reason 'saml-merge' and reference to assertion id.
- Update session store cleanup hook to remove transient roles with source != current_assertion_id.
- Add instrumentation to measure assertion-merge time and capture examples that change effective privileges.
- Coordinate with infra to allow a short feature flag rollout for the safer merge logic.
migration_plan: Migration is lightweight: new merge logic is backward compatible. For long-lived sessions we will run a one-off pass in staging that scans sessions for conflicting transient roles and emits normalization audit events. A migration script (safe-run) will be added to ops playbook to expire affected sessions for customers with confirmed incidents. Document the script and provide step-by-step rollback in the PR.
qa_plan:
- Unit tests for merge strategy and deny-first resolution.
- Integration tests simulating two IdPs with overlapping attributes.
- End-to-end tests in staging using recorded SAML assertions from customer escalations.
- SE verification checklist to confirm audit entries include pre/post snapshots and assertion IDs.
- Load test to ensure added audit writing at merge path does not degrade latency beyond SLO.
